audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep was described as flat sustain — 'her Q-W sustain out-trades you', 'W outer-cone true damage', 'healing the trade off W'. The half-and-half split was never stated, and it is the single most useful fact a melee champion can have here.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Camille blasts in a cone after a delay, dealing damage. Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille.' Standing in the inner half means no slow, no bonus damage and no heal for her. Ambessa is melee and already wants to be glued to Camille, so the correct play is to close the gap into the cone rather than back out of it — the opposite of what the page implied.
audit.corrected: whys[3], wants.foe[1] and breakdown.cooldowns now state that only the outer half slows, damages extra and heals her.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is titled 'Fight near walls' and its description read 'Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown' — the title's actual reason was never given anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's Hookshot text: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing.' No wall means no Hookshot: in the open middle of the lane she has no engage and no escape, and it is 16s at rank 1 down to 12s.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now state the terrain requirement and the 16s number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' said 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade' and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'the lane-control window: trade around Hookshot's cooldown and bank small leads', which contradicts the content layer calling 4-5 Ambessa's weakest window.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 Ambessa's Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s while Precision Protocol is 8-6s and Tactical Sweep 14-12s, so Camille simply gets more trades per minute.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now names Precision Protocol's 9s recast; phases[3].why states the cooldown mismatch and matches the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank'. The Hextech Ultimatum was never named or timed.
audit.why: The Hextech Ultimatum is 140s at rank 1, dashes to a target champion and anchors them to the area — it is the reason Camille's late game is an inescapable 1v1, and it is a cooldown Ambessa can count.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names both ultimates with their cooldowns and says what each actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: Adaptive Defenses was never mentioned in either layer, so the burst maths on the page is wrong by a shield every time.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Basic attacks on champions grant a shield equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type.' Ambessa deals almost entirely physical damage, so every auto Camille lands puts up a physical shield exactly as Ambessa's combo arrives, and it scales with Camille's health build rather than her damage build.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d now states that her autos pre-shield against physical.

notes: Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions of both say none of that, so I never claimed W grounds her Hookshot. _missing-interactions.json says 'Camille can go untargetable through your commit (The Hextech Ultimatum (R))' and her kit file carries an untargetable flag on R — Riot's own description is only 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area', with no untargetability in it. I treated that as a tooltip-parse misfire and wrote nothing about waiting out an untargetable phase, because telling a player to hold their combo for a phase that does not exist loses the fight outright. Riot's Hookshot text says 'knocking up', while the content layer calls it a stun in four places; I used knock up in the strings I rewrote. Camille is called 'he' in breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, breakdown.wave, report[4], report[8] and report[12] — boilerplate duplicates I did not spend edits on.
